[1/4] Plan ackermann win: direct-register multi-arg call args, then 2-param delta inlining

impact_assessment.why: The goal demands beating C and Rust on every committed benchmark, and ackermann is the last open case: Cairn 2.7-3.8x behind C because both inline paths require one-parameter functions, so all 25M calls stay real while gcc's 10-level self-inlining collapses the A(1,n)/A(2,n) shells into call-free loops
impact_assessment.benefits: L1 (direct-register simple args) removes the push/pop/movabs shuffle from every multi-arg call program-wide; L2 (2-param delta inlining: param0 constant-delta lea reads, param1 bound in one dedicated callee-saved register) eliminates the shell calls that dominate A(3,9) and closes the gap toward C
impact_assessment.risks: contract: inline copies must stay semantically identical including trap and overflow behavior; dependency: codegen 100-330 and 1190-1400, machine assembler opcodes; concurrency: none; state: README standings, ADR register, benchmark harness numbers
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first shape and e2e tests per lever, strict refusals (param rebind, non-return-tree body, arg1 forms outside literal/param+-imm/self-call, depth cap bounding the 2^d copy growth), interleaved harness runs 2-3x, gates and KB sync before commit
